title: Nvidia earnings, Anthropic's IPO could mean more trouble for bitcoin
excerpt: Amid Anthropic IPO hype and Nvidia earnings angst, bitcoin and other cryptos are exposed to new market headwinds this week.
content_html:
Why Nvidia and Anthropic could create new trouble for bitcoin

By Samuel O'Brient

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-17T17:49:47.083Z

Bitcoin has had a tough year, and two looming market events could make it a little tougher for the apex crypto.

Bitcoin prices recently plunged to a three month low, primarily driven by accelerating liquidations and a broader slowdown in the crypto space that's dragged the world's largest cryptocurrency nearly 30% in 2026.

But the crypto market may be facing two negative catalysts back-to-back this week.

Investors are preparing for Anthropic's hugely anticipating IPO, an expected to set records as the company eyes a $1.4 trillion valuation. Crypto pros have raised concerns about what the Anthropic IPO may mean for bitcoin, recalling a similar IPO that rocked markets earlier this year.

"Just as it did ahead of SpaceX's highly anticipated initial public offering in June, bitcoin (BTC) has sold off in the weeks before Anthropic's listing, reported for Thursday," said Thahbib Rahman, a research analyst at crypto analytics firm Block Scholes. "BTC fell 19% in the 50 days before SpaceX began trading, and it is down 23% over the same stretch today."

The Anthropic IPO isn't coming at a good time for bitcoin or for the broader crypto market. Despite rallying in August, bitcoin is down 27% year-to-date following the October Binance hack that triggered a cascade of selling in both crypto and crypto-linked stocks. Other leading cryptos such as ethereum and solana have fallen even further.

Now retail traders appear to be rotating out of bitcoin and other crypto investments in preparation for the Anthropic IPO, helping fuel the negative momentum pushing crypto prices lower.

Others who don't want to load up on shares may be more drawn to tokenized equities such as perpetual futures. or "perps," which let investors use platforms like Polymarket to bet on Anthropic's valuation and share price before the AI frontier lab begins trading on the Nasdaq.

Both scenarios could make it more difficult for bitcoin and its peers to recover, as they both threaten to drain but liquidity and trading interest out of the crypto market at a time when digital assets are already struggling.

The second headwind is coming from Nvidia, which is scheduled to report earnings after closing bell on Tuesday. Investors are waiting anxiously for anything that might offer insights into the future of the AI trade after CEO Jensen's resignation sent the stock into a tailspin.

Bitcoin moves in tandem with the Nasdaq 100, but following the recent tech sell-off, it may have further to fall if a disappointing earnings report from the chip maker causes more pressure on the tech trade. Investors may react by offloading risk assets such as crypto in a rush to flee into safer stores of value.

"The useful framing for this week is not 'IPO drains crypto,'" said Alice Liu, head of research at CoinMarketCap. "It is that two equity events, Nvidia on Tuesday and Anthropic on Thursday, will be traded around the clock on crypto venues by a market that has just had its leverage removed."
